provenance: Demonstration checklists and response steps written by Team ANGARIS for the prototype. They are not NASA EVA procedures and are not validated. Every interval is a demonstration value. The system only proposes; the commander decides and every decision is logged.

pre.text: Daily check-in completed today by every EVA crew member (FUTURE 01).
No symptom assessment is holding EVA participation for an EVA crew member (FUTURE 02).
Vital-sign check taken and reviewed for each EVA crew member.
Suit biomedical telemetry link tested with the intravehicular (IV) crew member.
pre.alternative: Telemetry unavailable: agree verbal status calls every 10 minutes (demonstration interval).

pre.text: Voice loop check with the IV crew member.
pre.alternative: Voice loop unavailable: agree hand signals and buddy checks; the commander decides whether the EVA can proceed.
Pressure readout unavailable: record that this check could not be done; the commander decides.

pre.text: Earth Link status noted. If the link is lost, the EVA runs under the autonomous protocol and every decision is logged on board.

during.text: Status call at each task milestone.
IV crew member watches suit biomedical telemetry.
during.alternative: Telemetry unavailable: verbal status call every 10 minutes (demonstration interval).

during.text: Any symptom reported by an EVA crew member is logged with the event buttons below.

post.text: Post-EVA symptom check for each EVA crew member (journal check-in or symptom assessment).

post.alternative: Pulse oximeter unavailable: ask the symptom questions and record that vital signs were not measured.

post.text: EVA log queued to Earth (sent automatically when the link is available).

events.label: EVA crew member reports feeling unwell

steps.text: Pause the current task and secure position (crew judgement).
Ask the crew member to describe the symptoms; the IV crew member logs the answers.
IV crew member reviews suit biomedical telemetry.
steps.alternative: Telemetry unavailable: verbal status every 2 minutes (demonstration interval).

steps.text: Commander decides: continue, or end the EVA and return to the airlock.
Urgent report queued to the ground medical team (sent when the link is available). Do not wait for the reply to act.
Switch to verbal status checks every 5 minutes (demonstration interval).
Record the time telemetry was lost.
Commander decides whether the EVA continues.
Use the agreed hand signals and buddy checks.
Both EVA crew members move to a safe position in sight of each other.
Commander decides whether to end the EVA.
Continue under the autonomous protocol: decisions are taken on board and logged.
Reports stay queued and are sent in priority order when the link returns.
